transcript.content: Hello. I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?

I'm here because I really need help dealing with a very stressful situation. I've realized that a certain organization has been monitoring my every move and constantly following me wherever I go. I just don't know how to make them stop, and I need your help.
Have you also been hearing any voices or seeing things that other people don't seem to notice?
No, I haven't heard any unusual voices or seen anything like that. My senses are perfectly fine, and I only see and hear what is actually happening around me.
How has your mood been through all of this? Have you had periods where you felt very depressed, or times when you felt unusually high, energetic, or irritable?

My mood has actually been relatively normal, despite all the stress. I haven't experienced any extreme highs, deep depressions, or unusual irritability. Aside from being anxious about being watched, my emotions feel quite stable.
Apart from the stress of being watched, how have you been managing with your daily responsibilities, like work, chores, or keeping up with friends?

Honestly, I manage my daily life and responsibilities just fine. I still go to work, keep up with my chores, and see my friends without any real issues. It's only when I notice them actively monitoring me that things get stressful, but otherwise, I function completely normally.
How long has this been going on? When did you first notice that this organization was monitoring you?
It started exactly two years and two months ago. I first noticed it when I realized the same people were following my commute every single day, and it hasn't stopped since then.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were Delusional Disorder and Schizophrenia. Schizophrenia is now ruled out because the patient has no other psychotic symptoms (such as hallucinations, disorganized speech, or negative symptoms) and their daily functioning and behavior remain completely intact and unimpaired outside of the delusion. This presentation of a persistent persecutory delusion lasting over two years with preserved functioning is characteristic of Delusional Disorder.
